## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Nivutakathā* (Kv 13.5) is a debate situated in the thirteenth chapter of the *Kathāvatthu* within the Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The text examines whether an individual who is obstructed or hindered (*nivuta*) can abandon the hindrances (*nīvaraṇa*) [Bareau 1955]. In his study of early Buddhist sectarian doctrines, André Bareau notes the opposing propositions debated on this theme: on the one side, the proposition that someone who is subject to hindrances does not abandon them—drawing analogies with the premise that an impassioned person (*ratta*) does not abandon passion (*rāga*), or an angry person hatred (*dosa*)—and on the other, the thesis that one who is enveloped and obstructed by hindrances can abandon them through the process of purification that must be realized [Bareau 1955].
SuttaCentral records one translation in one language and identifies citations or textual links with AN 4.47 (*Suvidūrasutta*), DN 2 (*Sāmaññaphala Sutta*), and other *Kathāvatthu* chapters including Kv 3.4, Kv 7.5, Kv 10.9, and Kv 13.7 [SuttaCentral]. Machine text-reuse data from DharmaNexus identifies 207 matching passages shared with 25 other Pali texts, demonstrating particularly strong internal reuse with structurally related debates in the *Kathāvatthu*, notably *Sammukhībhūtakathā* (Kv 13.6, with substantial overlap across §§0.1–5.10), *Paribhogamayapuññakathā* (Kv 7.5), *Samāpannoassādetikathā* (Kv 13.7), and *Samādānahetukathā* (Kv 10.9) [DharmaNexus]. In the Sutta and Abhidhamma literature, DharmaNexus aligns passages with AN 4.47 (confirming SuttaCentral's cross-reference), the *Bojjhaṅga Saṁyutta* (SN 46), the *Cūḷahatthipadopama Sutta* (MN 27), and the *Paṭṭhāna* (*Mahantaraduka*) [DharmaNexus]. It also notes a low-scoring cross-language match with the Tibetan *Āgamakṣudrakavyākhyāna* (D 4115) [DharmaNexus].
